This row's own case is named in the run: "ok metalchain_queue_label_is_nil" and "ok the_ports_own_queue_answers_as_apples_does" for the queue this scope records, and the scope itself is asked over the queue the case made. What is NOT verified on that guest, and why, is measured in the run's own lines: "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 2.0 on this guest: NIL" and "an EAGLContext over OpenGL ES 1.1 on this guest: NIL", so MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice answers nil there and every case that needs the port's device has no object to ask. The probe asks all fourteen constants in tests/backports/device/metalchain-expectations.h by name and prints ok / FAIL / NOT ANSWERED for each, so a reader can see which were reached (facts/Metal/CommandChain26.md)

entries.reason: the queue's only submit call, and it COMMITS: each buffer of the C array that this port made is committed through the queue underneath, which draws over the EAGL context; one from anywhere else is refused by name rather than sent to a queue that cannot read it. Apple's own -commit:count: RETURNS on the header's own path and on the un-ended one alike, measured in a process execed on its own (chain-commit.sh)
entries.effect: the commit returns and the port's own work is submitted; a buffer this port did not make is refused with a line naming its class. The run that placed the method on the queue measured this case as a FAILURE while it sat on CharonMetalDevice, and it is asked by the device probe on the guest; Held by the device probe tests/backports/device/metalchain-probe, whose runner refuses to run a stale binary by comparing LC_UUIDs built against installed, and whose run of 2026-10-04 on the emulated iPhone3,1 6.1.3 measured every case in tests/backports/device/metalchain-expectations.h (facts/Metal/CommandChain26.md)
